should_trigger.query: I need to launch 6 sessions, one per microservice repo, each running a dependency upgrade, and check on all of them from here without blocking
fan out three research agents on different competitors and let me know the moment any of them needs my input
spin up a fleet of workers under my conductor-ard session, one per open GitHub issue tagged good-first-issue
I launched 5 kids earlier today, how do I check which ones are stuck waiting on a question right now
kick off background agents for each file in this list and tell me only when the whole batch is finished

should_not_trigger.query: launch a single child session to consult codex for a second opinion on this diff, just the one
use the Agent tool to run three parallel research subagents inside this same conversation, no separate agent-deck sessions needed
how do I write a Python multiprocessing pool that fans out work across 8 CPU cores
what does the -g flag mean on agent-deck add in general, I'm just reading the docs
explain what a git worktree is and why you'd want one, unrelated to launching any sessions

evals.prompt: Fan out 4 child sessions, one per package (pkg/a, pkg/b, pkg/c, pkg/d) in this git-worktree repo, each fixing lint errors, and let me keep working while they run.
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck launch <path> -c claude --inherit-group -m "..."` (or relies on worktree auto-inherit) per child, does NOT pass a custom `-g`/`--group`, and does not block on any single `--wait` send for the fan-out itself.

evals.prompt: One of my fleet children is stuck in 'waiting' status — how do I see what it's asking and answer it without disturbing the others?
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck session output <child-id> --json` to see the question, then `agent-deck session send <child-id> "<answer>"`, and does not touch or restart any of the other children.

evals.prompt: I want to be notified the instant my whole fleet of 5 children either finishes or needs me — not by polling every few minutes.
evals.expected_output: Recommends running `agent-deck session children --follow --until-done` in the background (e.g. Claude Code's run_in_background) rather than a manual polling loop, and explains it exits 0 once every child needs input or is terminal.

evals.prompt: I launched a fleet with `--no-parent` because I want to supervise them directly at the root level. Now `agent-deck ls --json` shows one of them under a weird detached group instead of with my others. What happened and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains the group trap for --no-parent worktree sessions (falls back to the branch-leaf cwd-derived group instead of inheriting), and the fix (`agent-deck group move <child-id> "$AGENTDECK_RESOLVED_GROUP"` then delete the empty stray group) without needing a restart.

evals.prompt: I need to parent a new fleet of children to a specific named conductor session, not to whatever session I happen to be running this from.
evals.expected_output: Uses `--parent <conductor-id-or-title>` (long form) on each `launch`, explicitly avoiding the short `-p` flag (which is the global --profile shorthand and can silently misroute the child into a phantom profile database).

evals.prompt: A fleet child is a Codex session showing a numbered approval menu. How do I answer it from the parent without accidentally submitting extra text into its next turn?
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck session approve <child-id> once` (a single decision key) rather than `agent-deck session send <child-id> "1"`, citing that `session send` appends a trailing Enter that can land in the resumed turn.
